title: Dating the Overdue Period on Workplace Cafe Management Program Invoicing
content:
The account terms of the Workplace Cafe Management Program count the days overdue on a contract in calendar days. The period always closes on the day the charge is raised, that day itself being counted, and it always opens on the day after the ledger movement that fixes it. Which movement fixes it is settled by what the contract's ledger shows over the three months up to the day the charge is raised.

**The term as written.** Where a payment stands received on the contract in the three months up to the day the charge is raised and no service credit stands allowed over those three months, the days overdue run from the day after the payment most recently received up to and including the day the charge is raised; where a payment stands received over those three months and a service credit stands allowed over them, the days overdue run from the day after the service credit most recently allowed up to and including the day the charge is raised; and where no payment stands received over those three months, the days overdue run from the day after the management fee invoice most recently posted up to and including the day the charge is raised.

**The three months.** In each branch the three months are the three months up to the day the charge is raised, and the same three months are read for the payments received and for the service credits allowed.

**The two ends.** The day that opens the period is the day after the movement named, so the day of that movement is not itself counted; the day the charge is raised closes the period and is counted.

**A first hypothetical.** A charge raised on a hypothetical 2026-06-30, on a contract whose ledger shows a payment received on 2026-05-12 and no service credit allowed in the three months up to that day: the days overdue run from 2026-05-13 up to and including 2026-06-30, which is 49 calendar days.

**A second hypothetical.** The same contract and the same day, with a service credit most recently allowed on 2026-06-04 within those three months and the payment still standing: the days overdue run from 2026-06-05 up to and including 2026-06-30, which is 26 calendar days.

**A third hypothetical.** The same day again, with no payment received in the three months up to it and the management fee invoice most recently posted on 2026-04-01: the days overdue run from 2026-04-02 up to and including 2026-06-30, which is 90 calendar days.
